title: POC scoping: integration & benchmarks with Lumen DataWorks
summary: Redwood AE + SE run a detailed POC scoping with Lumen DataWorks. Discussion covered OpenAI-compatible SDK integration, function/tool calling, structured output, benchmark targets (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec), workload sizing (concurrent users, seq lengths), security requirements (VPC/KMS/SOC2), and timeline for a 6-week pilot. Agreed next steps: share benchmark spreadsheet, security packet, and schedule initial workload benchmark kickoff in one week.
topics: Security: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SSO
action_items: Samira: Share pilot pricing band and benchmark spreadsheet by 2026-09-02
Eli: Prepare Redwood test harness + seed prompts for Lumen's intents by 2026-09-03
Aiden Brooks (Lumen): Send SOC2 report and KMS architecture diagram by 2026-09-01
Tomás Ruiz (Lumen): Provide expected QPS and seq-length distribution CSV by 2026-09-02
Priya Narang: nominate internal eval owners and acceptance criteria by 2026-09-04
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark spreadsheet and security packet (SOC2, ISO summary)
Lumen to export workload traces and token distributions
Agree on canary success criteria: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms for 2k concurrent users with quantized model
Set up temporary VPC peering for pilot or use Redwood Private trial
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-29
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Eli Chen (Redwood SE), Nina Ortiz (Redwood Solutions), Jason Burke (Redwood Support); Mark Rutherford (Lumen CTO), Priya Narang (Head of ML), Tomás Ruiz (Infra), Hannah Lee (Product), Aiden Brooks (Security)

Summary (auto): quick POC scoping focused on integration approach (OpenAI-compat SDKs), benchmarks and success metrics, and security checklist.

00:00:12 Samira (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side - I'm Samira, I'm the AE. Eli is our senior SE, he'll cover the benchmark plan and test harness.
00:00:28 Mark (Lumen): Hey, Mark here. Thanks. We have Priya and Tomás and Aiden on. we have pretty tight timeline, so hoping to scope this clearly.
00:00:40 Eli (Redwood): Hi all. Quick agenda: discuss success criteria, map workload, choose integration path (OpenAI-compatible endpoints vs native SDK), and outline the pilot steps for the next 6 weeks.
00:01:03 Priya (Lumen): Our main ask: replace current third-party endpoint for conversational summarization and ticket triage. success = 95% of top-1 label accuracy and lower cost per 1k requests, and latency under production thresholds.
00:01:26 Samira (Redwood): Good. can you share current numbers? p50/p95, qps, avg tokens?
00:01:35 Tomás (Lumen): We have some roughs: p50 ~ 160ms, p95 ~ 700ms with our current hosted provider at 1k concurrent. avg prompt length 220 tokens, completion avg 80 tokens. spikes hit 2k concurrent at peak.
00:02:04 Eli (Redwood): ok that's helpful. for the pilot we should get a sample of the real token distribution — that lets our runtime pick kernels and batching strategy. any constraints around VPC or private networking?
00:02:22 Aiden (Lumen): Security is key. We need SSO + SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration for keys. also SOC2 evidence. we're evaluating dedicated vs hosted.
00:02:36 Nina (Redwood): We can do VPC peering for Redwood Private or provide a dedicated lane via Dedicated pools. both support KMS/HSM integrations. we'll include the security packet.
00:02:52 Hannah (Lumen): One question: we rely on function calling to trigger downstream services — will Redwood support the same tool-calling semantics as our current OpenAI-style flow?
00:03:07 Eli (Redwood): Yes, we have OpenAI-compatible endpoints and the SDK supports function/tool calling and structured outputs. there's a small differences sometimes in schema enforcement; we'll demo mapping.
00:03:25 Mark (Lumen): And about structured output — we need strict JSON outputs for ingestion. if the model drifts, we need validators and fallback.
00:03:38 Eli (Redwood): We recommend schema-first approaches: prompt guards + post-parse validators in the SDK. Redwood Optimize can run checks and alert on regressions in structured fields.
00:03:55 Samira (Redwood): Let's walk through pilot success criteria. Priya, you mentioned labels; anything else?
00:04:06 Priya (Lumen): Yes: 1) Top-1 label accuracy >= 95% across a holdout set, 2) end-to-end latency p50 < 120ms and p95 < 450ms for our baseline 2k concurrent load, 3) cost per 1k tokens reduced by at least 20%, and 4) no PII leakage or unlogged exposures.
00:04:33 Eli (Redwood): Those look reasonable. p95 target is aggressive but achievable with quantization and caching. important: is the 2k concurrency sustained or bursty?
00:04:45 Tomás (Lumen): It's bursty — sustained at 800-1k, but bursts up to 2k during weekday peaks.
00:04:54 Eli (Redwood): Great — our test harness can simulate burst patterns. we'll run mixed latency/throughput tests and report both p50/p95 and tokens/sec.
00:05:09 Mark (Lumen): Can you support warm KV cache priming? our current provider doesn't do prefix caching well.
00:05:18 Eli (Redwood): Redwood runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; we can prime caches during canary runs. sometimes transcriptions have it as KV cash — humor — but yes, we do.
00:05:32 Hannah (Lumen): For integration — would you recommend using the OpenAI-compatible endpoints or native SDK? we want minimal dev effort.
00:05:44 Nina (Redwood): If you already use OpenAI-style calls, the OpenAI-compatible endpoints are lowest friction. SDK adds helper structs for function calling and structured output validation. either works.
00:06:02 Priya (Lumen): We have some tooling baked into our backend that assumes specific OpenAI response shapes. migrating to Redwood's SDK might be extra work. so prefer endpoint parity first.
00:06:16 Eli (Redwood): That's fine — we guarantee endpoint parity for the features you need: streaming, function calling, and structured responses. small differences in field names can be shimmed by middleware.
00:06:30 Aiden (Lumen): On encryption, do you support CMEK with customer KMS?
00:06:36 Jason (Redwood): Yes — Dedicated and Private options support CMEK. we'll include KMS integration notes.
00:06:48 Mark (Lumen): Ok next: benchmarks. what are Redwood's standard benchmarks for these workloads?
00:06:55 Eli (Redwood): We measure p50/p95 token latency, tokens/sec, and throughput at various seq lengths. For POC we'll run: baseline small-scale, then scale to your target concurrency with burst profiles. we'll also measure tail latency on streaming responses.
00:07:15 Priya (Lumen): Do you have an existing harness? we can't leak production data into external systems.
00:07:23 Eli (Redwood): We have a test harness that runs locally or in your cloud via a small runner. you can run the agent inside your VPC to keep traces local; only aggregated metrics come back if you opt in.
00:07:38 Tomás (Lumen): Good. we'll prefer a runner in our VPC. we'll need docs to set it up.
00:07:45 Samira (Redwood): We'll send the runner repo + setup instructions.
00:07:52 Mark (Lumen): About model variants — do you recommend quantized models for the p95 targets?
00:07:58 Eli (Redwood): For latency/cost goals, yes. quantization plus our batcher reduces cost and keeps p95 low. we should validate quality doesn't regress — Redwood Optimize can run A/B evals on your prompts.
00:08:12 Priya (Lumen): We care about hallucinations in summary tasks. what's your approach to measuring quality?
00:08:19 Eli (Redwood): We'll use a holdout set and run automatic metrics (ROUGE/BLEU where appropriate) and custom classifier checks. plus human evals for a subset.
00:08:36 Hannah (Lumen): Can we instrument quality alerts for structured output violations?
00:08:40 Nina (Redwood): Yes — the Console supports schema mismatch alerts, and alerts can integrate with your PagerDuty or Slack.
00:08:51 Aiden (Lumen): compliance question: will audit logs show per-token access and redaction?
00:08:58 Jason (Redwood): Audit logs include request IDs, headers, model version, and can include redacted payloads depending on retention settings. we'll send a details doc.
00:09:12 Mark (Lumen): Cool. timeline — we want a 6-week pilot window, is that feasible?
00:09:20 Samira (Redwood): Yes. week 0: scope + data exchange. week 1: infra setup + runner. week 2: baseline runs. week 3: optimize quantization and batching. week 4: canary at 30% traffic. week 5: full pilot evaluation and handoff.
00:09:38 Priya (Lumen): That matches our internal sprint cadence. who needs to be involved from our side?
00:09:45 Mark (Lumen): infra (Tomás), ML (Priya), security (Aiden), product (Hannah).
00:09:52 Eli (Redwood): From our side: SE lead (Eli), support (Jason), solutions (Nina), AE (Samira).
00:10:04 Tomás (Lumen): For workload sizing we'll export traces — they include sequence lengths and user session IDs. is CSV ok?
00:10:12 Eli (Redwood): CSV is perfect. include timestamps to recreate burst patterns.
00:10:20 Priya (Lumen): One more: function calling — we wire tool calls to internal microservices. we need to ensure timeouts and retries are preserved if calls are proxied through Redwood.
00:10:33 Eli (Redwood): Our function calling supports a tool invocation model where the model returns a JSON payload. you run the tool locally; Redwood won't proxy your internal services. for calls that need remote tools we can help design safe proxies.
00:10:49 Hannah (Lumen): So we keep our tool endpoints internal and use the model to return JSON, then our code calls the services?
00:10:56 Eli (Redwood): Exactly. that preserves security boundaries.
00:11:04 Mark (Lumen): Edge case: sometimes model returns slightly malformed JSON; do you provide auto-correction or strict parsing?
00:11:12 Nina (Redwood): SDK includes schema validators and a retry-with-prompt-fix flow. we can also include guardrails in the prompt to enforce JSON.
00:11:25 Priya (Lumen): Great. Cost: do you have price estimates for Dedicated vs Hosted for our expected throughput?
00:11:33 Samira (Redwood): We'll share a pricing band. roughly, hosted is lower startup cost but higher marginal; Dedicated gives predictable unit cost at scale. we'll include exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
00:11:46 Aiden (Lumen): About data retention — we need 90-day logs and the ability to disable retention for content.
00:11:53 Jason (Redwood): You can configure retention per route; Private deployments can have no retention. we'll include config options.
00:12:02 Tomás (Lumen): Ok, drill into the benchmark plan briefly — what metrics will you produce?
00:12:10 Eli (Redwood): We'll provide: p50/p95 latency per model variant, tokens/sec, throughput at target concurrency, memory utilization, GPU occupancy, and cost-per-1k tokens. plus structured-output error rates and top-1 accuracy on holdout.
00:12:28 Mark (Lumen): That covers it. who will run the initial benchmark?
00:12:33 Eli (Redwood): We'll run jointly. Redwood will prepare the harness and starter configs, you run it in your VPC runner. our SE will observe and adjust.
00:12:42 Priya (Lumen): On acceptance criteria: if top-1 accuracy is 94.5% do we fail or pass?
00:12:50 Samira (Redwood): We should define a pass/fail band and a mitigation plan. e.g., 94-95% = conditional pass with tuning; <94% = fail and iterate. we'll add this to the acceptance doc.
00:13:07 Hannah (Lumen): For function calling latency, do you measure model side only or E2E?
00:13:13 Eli (Redwood): Both. model inference latency is separate; we will also measure E2E with your tool invocation times included.
00:13:24 Mark (Lumen): Any limitations around OpenAPI specs for structured outputs?
00:13:30 Nina (Redwood): We accept OpenAPI-style schemas; SDK can coerce model outputs to schema and return parse errors for monitoring.
00:13:42 Tomás (Lumen): Logging and PII redaction again — can we have a demo of redaction?
00:13:48 Jason (Redwood): We'll include a short video/gif and doc showing automated redaction in Console.
00:13:56 Priya (Lumen): Good. A thought: we route certain tenants to lower-latency Dedicated pools. can Redwood route by tenant via headers?
00:14:05 Eli (Redwood): Yes, smart routing by policy (tenant header) is supported — you can pin tenants to Dedicated capacity or region.
00:14:15 Mark (Lumen): Ok next: schedule. when can you send the security packet and benchmark spreadsheet?
00:14:20 Samira (Redwood): We'll send both within 48 hours. so by 2026-09-02.
00:14:28 Aiden (Lumen): We'll review and get back. also will provide SOC2 and our KMS diagram by 2026-09-01.
00:14:35 Priya (Lumen): let's record owners: Priya will own quality, Tomás infra.
00:14:40 Samira (Redwood): noted — we'll include a RACI in the kickoff email.
00:14:47 Mark (Lumen): Anything else?
00:14:50 Hannah (Lumen): One more — can we try function call cases where model needs to call multiple tools in sequence?
00:14:58 Eli (Redwood): yes, our orchestrations support multi-step tool calls via the SDK; we'll provide examples.
00:15:06 Samira (Redwood): Ok quick recap of next steps: Redwood sends security + benchmark sheet; Lumen sends traces and SOC2; schedule benchmark kickoff for week of 2026-09-06 or 09-08. action items captured.
00:15:22 Mark (Lumen): thanks. we'll review and sync.
00:15:27 Samira (Redwood): Thanks everyone.

(There is a brief pause and some side chatter)

00:35:01 Priya (Lumen): sorry one more thing — on model rollouts, do you support canary traffic split and automatic fallback to a previous model if accuracy drops?
00:35:10 Eli (Redwood): Yes, rollouts with automatic regress detect are supported. you can configure thresholds tied to prompt sets; if threshold breached we automatically route to fallback variant.
00:35:24 Tomás (Lumen): That would be helpful for nights/weekends.
00:35:29 Nina (Redwood): We'll show the rollout UI during the kickoff.
00:35:35 Aiden (Lumen): security from infra: do you do penetration tests on Private deployments?
00:35:42 Jason (Redwood): Yes, Private deployments can be part of our pentest engagement; we can share prior reports under NDA.
00:35:50 Mark (Lumen): Great. any blockers left?
00:35:54 Priya (Lumen): none on our side besides data export timing.
00:36:00 Samira (Redwood): We'll follow up in email with dates and the initial configs. thanks everyone.

00:53:58 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears: 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'KV cash', 'quantization' sometimes split 'quanti zation', speaker labels may be approximate.
